title: VidUEU-Agent: A Data-Curation Agent for Multimodal Understanding, Editing, and Unified Tasks
excerpt: The advancement of multimodal learning is heavily constrained by the scarcity and high annotation cost of high-quality instruction data. While raw videos offer an abundant and dynamic source of visual knowledge, transforming them into precise instruction data remains highly challenging. To bridge this gap, we present VidUEU-Agent, an automated pipeline that synthesizes instruction data from raw videos for multimodal understanding, editing, and unified tasks. VidUEU-Agent follows a four-stage pipeline: it performs global perception to filter low-quality shots, mines keyframes and multimodal signals, constructs metadata and routes the metadata to synthesize instruction samples. More…

ai.summary: VidUEU‑Agent is an automated pipeline that converts raw video footage into high‑quality multimodal instruction data for tasks like understanding, editing, and unified multimodal processing, using a four‑stage process to curate the data.
ai.why: It lowers the barrier for creating large instruction datasets, allowing developers to train better multimodal models without costly manual annotation.

title: Axion 1.0: Open Agent Foundation Models, Simplified
excerpt: We introduce Axion 1.0, a fully open agent foundation model that combines strong and broad agentic capabilities with a remarkably simple training recipe. Axion 1.0 is trained in only three stages: two lightweight supervised fine-tuning stages followed by reinforcement learning, without dedicated mid-training, direct preference optimization (DPO), or on-policy distillation (OPD). The first SFT stage develops strong self-contained reasoning through model-aware data construction, where we synthesize challenging problems and adversarially strengthen them based on the base model's own successful solution strategies. The second stage extends these capabilities to tool-dependent reasoning through…

ai.summary: Axion 1.0 is an open‑source agent foundation model trained with only three stages—two lightweight supervised fine‑tuning steps and a final reinforcement‑learning phase—omitting DPO and on‑policy distillation.
ai.why: Its simple training pipeline makes it easier for developers to reproduce or extend agent models without complex intermediate steps.

title: Behind Video Generation: Observations and Insights on Multimodal Understanding from Kling
excerpt: Video generation has progressed from isolated clips to coherent short-form audiovisual sequences, and the bottleneck is shifting from rendering to semantic control. This report summarizes the observations and insights on multimodal understanding gained from successive generations of Kling. We argue that generation quality is the projection of multimodal understanding through the entire data--conditioning--alignment--evaluation chain, and we examine this chain module by module. Kling-MLLM, a shared multimodal foundation model that unifies image, video, audio, synchronized audio--video, and interleaved inputs, is specialized for each downstream module. Because a DiT is trained on far fewer…

ai.summary: The report analyzes the Kling video generation system, highlighting how each stage—from data to conditioning, alignment, and evaluation—affects multimodal understanding and semantic control.
ai.why: Understanding these bottlenecks helps developers improve video generation pipelines and align models more effectively.

title: Factorized MLLM Embeddings for Composed Image Retrieval
excerpt: Composed Image Retrieval (CIR) aims to retrieve a target image given a reference image and a modification text. Although recent approaches leveraging Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have shown significant progress, we argue that the MLLM's compositional understanding remains underutilized. This stems from directly mapping composed queries into a retrieval embedding via contrastive supervision alone, without explicitly resolving the intended visual modifications. In this work, we introduce Factorized MLLM Embeddings (FactEmbed), which decouples compositional query comprehension from building discriminative embeddings. Rather than directly projecting the composed query into a single…

ai.summary: The paper proposes factorized embeddings for multimodal large language models that separate visual and textual components to improve composed image retrieval, where a reference image and modification text are used to find a target image.
ai.why: Improved embeddings can be integrated into retrieval systems, giving developers better performance on search‑by‑example and text‑guided image queries.

title: MoLRSI: A Recursive Self-Improving AI agent for Molecular Discovery
excerpt: Molecular discovery requires navigating vast combinatorial search spaces while balancing competing biological objectives. AI agents can automate expert-defined molecular design protocols, but automation alone does not address how to optimize workflows for new tasks or improve their development through experience. Here we introduce MoLRSI, an AI agent that combines systematic optimization of workflows and model architectures with persistent cross-task memory to recursively improve its search policy for molecular discovery. Workflow performance, refinement outcomes, and execution feedback guide subsequent searches, allowing the agent to improve both its workflows and its strategy for…

ai.summary: The paper introduces MoLRSI, a recursive self‑improving AI agent for molecular discovery that optimizes workflows and model architectures while retaining cross‑task memory.
ai.why: It demonstrates a new approach for building AI agents that continuously improve their scientific search processes.

title: SpecPilot: Autonomous Algorithm Discovery and Systems Optimization for Speculative Decoding
excerpt: Speculative decoding accelerates memory-bound LLM decoding with a lightweight drafter, and parallel drafters extend this speedup by drafting a whole block in one forward pass. However, it remains unclear whether their released systems (stock) attain the full speedup that parallel drafting permits. We identify three challenges. First, with one request, each step accepts few tokens but reads every target weight. Second, with batching, per-request verification work roughly halves the speedup over autoregressive (AR) decoding. Third, speculative decoding is deployment-specific, and no universal optimization fits every serving regime, drafter, target model and GPU. To address these challenges…

ai.summary: The "SpecPilot" system automates algorithm discovery and system optimization for speculative decoding, addressing challenges in token‑wise weight reads and verification overhead to improve LLM decoding speed.
ai.why: Offers a framework developers can use to accelerate LLM inference via more efficient speculative decoding pipelines.

title: ParetoSaddler: Pareto-Guided Optimization of Agent Harnesses for Quality and Cost
excerpt: Harness optimization can substantially improve LLM agents without modifying model weights, but existing methods primarily optimize response quality. Extending them to joint quality--cost optimization introduces a challenge: applying the deployment preference during intermediate updates can prematurely reject candidates that are valuable for later improvements. We introduce ParetoSaddler, which addresses this mismatch by separating intermediate candidate promotion from final deployment selection. At each iteration, an optimizer updates a parent harness to produce a candidate, and then compares the two over repeated executions and uses Bayesian bootstrap Pareto support to promote candidates…

ai.summary: ParetoSaddler introduces a Pareto‑guided optimization method for LLM agent harnesses that jointly considers response quality and deployment cost, separating intermediate candidate promotion from final selection to avoid premature rejection.
ai.why: Developers can use it to fine‑tune agents for both performance and cost efficiency, important for production deployments.

title: EvoTeam: Multi-Agent Collaboration via Evolving Teams
excerpt: LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) rely on collaboration among specialized agents to solve complex tasks. Existing methods improve MAS by refining the prompts, skills, and execution strategies of individual agents based on task feedback. However, improving individual agents does not necessarily lead to better team collaboration. Recent studies have therefore extended evolution to the collaboration level, using collective execution experience to adjust team organization, and inter-agent interactions. Nevertheless, evolving collaboration across heterogeneous tasks remains challenging, as existing approaches often constrain team reorganization within a shared structure and reuse interaction…

ai.summary: EvoTeam presents a method for evolving the organization of LLM‑based multi‑agent teams, using collective execution experience to adjust team structures and inter‑agent interactions rather than just individual agent prompts.
ai.why: Team‑level evolution can yield more effective collaborative agents, offering a new avenue for developers to improve complex task solving.

title: MoviEdit: Long-form Multi-Shot Video Editing Made Easy
excerpt: Long-form multi-shot video editing requires an intended edit to remain coherent across abrupt changes in scene, viewpoint, and subject appearance, while processing substantially longer visual context than conventional single-shot editors. We introduce MoviEdit, an end-to-end framework for scalable long-form multi-shot video editing that jointly addresses the challenges of data, modeling, and evaluation. To provide cross-shot supervision data at scale, we develop automatic data-generation pipelines spanning synchronized multi-view footage, real-world multi-shot videos, and generated multi-shot content, yielding 87K paired editing videos without manual annotation. Architecturally, MoviEdit…

ai.summary: MoviEdit introduces an end‑to‑end system for editing long‑form, multi‑shot videos by generating cross‑shot supervision data automatically and training a scalable model to maintain edit coherence across scene changes.
ai.why: Developers building video editing tools can leverage its data pipeline and model design to support longer, more complex video edits with less manual labeling.

title: YANAMI: A Large-Scale Multimodal Dataset and Benchmark for Multiturn Stateful Interaction
excerpt: Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) integrate visual understanding, generation, and editing within a single unified framework. However, existing unified multimodal datasets and benchmarks remain dominated by single-turn tasks. Even in recent multi-turn datasets, many turns can be solved independently without tracking information across turns. Consequently, they provide limited supervision and evaluation for multimodal stateful interaction, which requires models to understand, maintain, update, and faithfully realize evolving dialogue states across turns. To address this gap, we introduce YANAMI, the first large-scale multimodal dialogue dataset and benchmark for stateful interaction…

ai.summary: YANAMI introduces a large‑scale multimodal dataset and benchmark focused on multiturn, stateful interactions, requiring models to maintain and update visual and textual context across dialogue turns.
ai.why: The benchmark pushes developers toward building unified models that can handle ongoing, context‑aware multimodal conversations.

title: Are Frontier VLM Agents Ready to Be Robot Generalists? An Empirical Study with the Embodied Agent Arena
excerpt: A robot generalist must interpret a scene, act on it, and satisfy every condition of a task. How far do frontier vision-language models (VLMs) meet these demands? We introduce Embodied Agent Arena, evaluating ten VLM agents across Geometry, Spatial Reasoning, Affordance, Task Planning, and Manipulation. Its 1,000 cases combine 32 established sources with GeoProbe, our 168-case benchmark for camera, motion, depth, and scale estimation. A minimal harness leaves task decisions to the model through source-native interfaces. Closed-weight models lead all five domains, whereas open-weight VLMs show useful spatial reasoning but substantially lower planning and manipulation success. Beneath these…

ai.summary: Embodied Agent Arena evaluates ten vision‑language model agents on 1,000 embodied tasks across geometry, spatial reasoning, affordance, task planning, and manipulation, including a new 168‑case GeoProbe benchmark for camera, motion, depth, and scale estimation.
ai.why: It provides a concrete benchmark for measuring how well VLMs can act in real‑world robotic scenarios, useful for developers building embodied AI.

title: Think Less, Locally: Local Preference Learning for Reasoning Compression
excerpt: Large reasoning models achieve strong performance on challenging tasks, but their long chain-of-thought often incurs substantial inference costs by continuing to deliberate after sufficient information has been obtained. Existing reasoning compression methods primarily operate on reasoning trajectories, paying less attention to the local decision of whether further reasoning is necessary given the current state. We propose LoCo, a local preference learning method for reasoning compression. LoCo detects candidate overthinking states from the model's own traces, freezes the corresponding reasoning prefixes, regenerates shorter verified continuations from the same states, and trains on the…

ai.summary: LoCo introduces local preference learning to decide early when a reasoning chain can stop, reducing inference cost by avoiding unnecessary continuation of chain‑of‑thought reasoning.
ai.why: Developers can integrate LoCo to cut compute costs for large reasoning models while preserving answer quality.

title: Route Anything: A Study of Model and Policy Routing for General-Purpose AI Systems
excerpt: Artificial general intelligence (AGI) requires a method that can understand, generate, reason, and act across diverse domains and modalities. Rather than relying on a single model to master every capability, a promising path toward AGI now is to orchestrate a heterogeneous ecosystem of specialized models, tools, and policies (candidates) into a unified AI system. At the heart of this vision lies a fundamental question: how can an AI system dynamically select and coordinate the most capable candidate for each task while balancing performance and computational cost? In this work, we present Route Anything, a unified framework for studying model and policy routing across general-purpose AI…

ai.summary: The paper proposes a framework that routes queries to a heterogeneous set of specialized models, tools, and policies rather than a single monolithic model, aiming to improve general‑purpose AI performance across domains and modalities.
ai.why: It suggests a modular architecture developers can adopt to combine best‑of‑breed models for specific tasks, potentially reducing compute and improving capability coverage.

title: WebHarbor: Docking Real Websites for Evolving GUI Agent Environments
excerpt: GUI web agents require realistic and interactive environments that remain stable during both evaluation and training. Live website evaluation suffers from changing content, access restrictions, and limited coverage of authenticated workflows, while existing synthetic environments for training often lack functional depth and visual fidelity. We propose WebHarbor, a suite of 153 executable and dockerized website environments that faithfully reconstruct the visual interfaces, content, and functional workflows of real-world web services under deterministic control. We build WebHarbor through task-driven human-agent collaboration, where environments evolve as new tasks expand their functional…

ai.summary: WebHarbor provides 153 dockerized, executable website environments that faithfully reproduce visual interfaces, content, and functionality, enabling stable training and evaluation of GUI web agents.

excerpt: Psychotherapy clients may experience distress before they can coherently describe it, and their expression changes with emotion, perceived safety, and trust. We propose Pandora, a psychotherapy client simulation framework that models how psychological experience becomes situated, individual expression. excerpt: Large language models are deployed as long-horizon agents that compose diverse tools across MCP services into executable workflows. title: DreamX: Video Diffusion Model is a Universal Latent Action Learner
excerpt: Learning a universal action representation from video requires modeling dynamics that are consistent across different executions of the same action yet invariant to changes in embodiment and appearance. Existing latent action models infer actions from visual transitions, but their representations often entangle the underlying action with irrelevant visual variations, limiting transfer across embodiments. We introduce DreamX, which repurposes a pretrained video diffusion model as a universal latent action learner.
